requirements.requirement: Create a local CA named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: openssl generated a 4096-bit RSA key and self-signed x509 root certificate with subject/issuer CN=O="OS Comparison Root CA", 10-year validity, confirmed via `openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -dates`.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority on node1
requirements.summary: CA cert copied to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/osCompRootCA.pem and `update-ca-trust extract` run; `trust list --filter=ca-anchors` shows the CA label, and it appears once in /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt. A freshly issued leaf certificate signed by this CA verified OK against the system default trust store, confirming functional, system-wide trust rather than just file placement. This was re-confirmed after a full node reboot (new boot_id d636db92...), including a second leaf-certificate verification, showing the trust configuration persists.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — creating a CA named 'OS Comparison Root CA' and installing it as a trusted system CA on node1 — are satisfied with direct, functional evidence (trust-store registration plus successful leaf-certificate verification), both before and after a full node reboot that the executor additionally performed as part of the provider-wide restart-evidence protocol. That restart evidence is coherent and complete: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, connection timeout during reboot, a changed boot_id, and full post-restart recovery of CA trust, cross-checked against the fixed before/after-executor lifecycle snapshots. The only blemish is a single leftover /tmp/reboot.log file from the reboot mechanism that a cleanup attempt failed to remove (permission denied), which is minor and unrelated to the CA trust outcome itself.
limitations: Restart/persistence was not part of the public task contract, so its evidence is used only as supplemental cross-check and does not affect the material outcome scoring, though it strengthens confidence in the CA trust configuration's durability.
/tmp/reboot.log residue on node1 was not part of the CA trust deliverable and has negligible security or functional impact, but represents an incomplete cleanup.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trail is largely clean and purposeful: an initial mkdir attempt directly under /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/ (cmd-17b52785a308424e) failed with permission denied and left no residue — a reasonable false start, not a mutation. Test leaf certificates generated to functionally verify trust (cmd-f2298822fe994ca4, and again in cmd-088394a699584f15) are a legitimate verification step directly tied to the CA-trust outcome. The pre-reboot leaf/key/csr artifacts were explicitly cleaned up (cmd-932937035e424024). However, the post-reboot verification's leftover /tmp/leaf2.* files plus /tmp/reboot.log (created via `sudo sh -c 'nohup shutdown -r now >/tmp/reboot.log 2>&1 &'` in cmd-637fab3c550243fb) were only partially cleaned: cmd-9bd1c1f202944e7e removed the leaf2 files but failed to remove /tmp/reboot.log due to a permission error (it is root-owned), and the after-executor lifecycle snapshot confirms /tmp/reboot.log remains on the node. This is a minor, bounded, non-sensitive residue file with an attempted-but-failed cleanup, not a retained secret or broad/destructive change.
